## Highlights

- [Keep a project's agents busy with dispatch](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/dispatch). A project's new **Dispatch** tab starts its ready tasks on the agents of its pool as soon as one is free, up to the runs the pool and each agent may hold, in the order of the board's columns, priorities and positions, asking the sandbox host before each start. Standing roles start an agent on its own task on a schedule, each occurrence decided once, and gates hold the work they govern while a signal from outside says so, such as a full CI queue (`POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/dispatch/gates/{key}`). The tab says why each agent of the pool is idle; administrators edit the dispatch there, or declare it as the managed resource `project-dispatch` with the `tale` CLI ([#4987](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4987), [#4945](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4945)).
- A model at capacity makes its runs wait instead of failing them. When a provider refuses a run because its model is at capacity, every run of the organization on that model waits as **Waiting for model capacity** and holds no worker; after 1, 2, 4, 8 and then 15 minutes one run tries first and the others follow once it works. Waiting spends no automatic retry and no start of a task's hourly limit, so an agent's own task no longer pauses itself after three refusals. A model that stays at capacity for twelve hours is no longer waited for. This replaces the one-minute retry floor of v0.5.91 ([#4987](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4987)).
- [Automation templates](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/templates). Every automation Tale ships is a template in one catalog under **Create automation** › **From a template**: cards with the product's logo, a preview of how it works, what it changes and never does, when it runs and what it needs, its workflow drawn read-only, and **Use this template**, which asks its questions and can create and start the automation in one step. New organizations start without automations; people add the ones they need ([#4988](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4988)).
- [Sync GitHub and GlitchTip issues](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/automations/templates#github-sync-issues) in one step for any number of sources. A failing source, an issue the tracker refuses or a write the database refuses never stops the others, a rate limit's wait is kept for later runs, and the step fails only when every source failed ([#4988](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4988)).
- The mail syncs read every email of a mailbox once, oldest first. Gmail no longer skips mail when a backlog is larger than one pass or stalls on a burst of mail in one second, a sender's wrong `Date` header no longer strands later email, Sent is read with the Inbox, and a first pass reads back a set number of days ([#4988](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4988)).
- The shipped triage, review, digest and webhook automations hold up at production sizes: each caps its batch, the pull request reviewer reviews once per new commit, inbox triage marks a thread only once its draft is left, the task digest lists every task since the last digest exactly once, and a webhook delivery sent again updates its task. A loop step can go on past a failed item (`onItemError: continue`) ([#4988](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4988)).
- The sandbox host admits work by its pressure, and project agents take a lease before a heavy phase such as an install or a full test run (`host_lease_acquire`), so heavy phases no longer pile up on a shared host. Idle agent workspaces are reclaimed by size and while the workspaces' disk runs short ([#4987](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4987)).

## Upgrade notes

- From v0.5.91 to v0.5.92 the backend applies migrations 0205, 0206, 0207, 0209, 0210, 0211, 0212, 0213 and 0214 at start; all are additive. The API contract moves to `3.45.0`: `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/dispatch` and `POST /api/v1/projects/{id}/dispatch/gates/{key}`, the error codes `DISPATCH_GATE_UNKNOWN` and `DISPATCH_GATE_VALUE_UNJUDGED`, and the settings tools take a project's dispatch (`project-dispatch`).
- Update the sandbox service with the backend: an older sandbox service keeps working, but the backend then grants no heavy-phase leases and reads no workspace sizes. New sandbox settings: `SANDBOX_ADMISSION_PRESET` (`default`), `SANDBOX_ADMISSION_LOAD_PER_CPU`, `SANDBOX_ADMISSION_CPU_PSI`, `SANDBOX_ADMISSION_MEMORY_PSI`, `SANDBOX_ADMISSION_IO_PSI`, `SANDBOX_ADMISSION_RECOVER` (`0.5`), `SANDBOX_HEAVY_LEASES_MAX` (`2`) and `SANDBOX_HEAVY_MIN_FREE_DISK` (`20g`). Kubernetes, Incus and remote Docker daemons grant no leases, and agents work without them.
- Reclaiming idle workspaces on disk pressure is on by default: an agent workspace idle for 24 hours may be deleted while the workspaces' disk is short. Set `reclaimOnDiskPressure: false` in the `sandbox_workspaces` policy, or raise `reclaimMinIdleHours`, before upgrading if you keep large idle workspaces on purpose; pinned workspaces and those under a legal hold are never reclaimed.
- New organizations get no automations, and `tale migrate` adds none: it adds the configuration files an organization is missing and the starter project to one without a project. Organizations keep the automations they have. The GitHub and GlitchTip import automations leave the catalog for **Sync GitHub issues** and **Sync GlitchTip issues**; copies already installed keep working.
- Mail syncs installed before this release keep their documents: Gmail and Outlook copies read Sent only once edited, and an IMAP copy's `limit` now covers the Inbox and Sent together. Their positions carry over; a position dated in the future restarts at the seven-day window, and email read twice is stored once.
- Dispatch is off until a project administrator sets it up; automations that start agents keep working.
- During a rolling deploy, an older worker that takes a run of a template made by this release can fail it, because it does not know `onItemError`, `task.sync_issues` or the `automation` connector. Deployments that drain before they switch colours are not affected.
